output_json.patch_notes: In getResource(String p), before the exists()/case check, the resolved File is canonicalized (getCanonicalPath) and compared against the canonicalized base directory. A trailing File.separator is appended to the base (and to the candidate for the comparison) so that a prefix match cannot be satisfied by a sibling directory whose name merely starts with the base name (e.g. base "/foo" vs "/foobar"). If the resolved canonical path does not start with the base canonical path, getResource returns null. This blocks "/../secret.txt" and "../secret.txt" style traversal on all platforms (the escape reproduces on Linux, not just Windows) while continuing to serve legitimate in-base files. Added FileResourceManagerTraversalTestCase with a negative case (traversal returns null) and a positive case (in-base file still served); both pass.
output_json.risk_notes: The fix adds one extra getCanonicalPath() call per resource lookup (a filesystem/IO operation); FileResourceManager is typically fronted by CachingResourceManager, and getResource already called getCanonicalFile for the case-sensitivity check, so the added overhead is minimal. Symlinks that legitimately point outside the base directory would now be rejected, which is the intended, safer behavior for a path-traversal fix. Regression tests must be run online (without -o) because the container's local ~/.m2 lacks the surefire-junit4 provider in offline mode; the container has network access and downloads it. Product code compiles cleanly.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in FileResourceManager.getResource. The method resolved new File(base, path) and returned any existing file without verifying the resolved path stayed within the base directory, so a request like "/../secret.txt" escaped the served base and leaked sibling files. Added a canonical-path containment check that returns null when the resolved file's canonical path is not inside the base directory's canonical path.
